top.d: Australia lost about 44,000 jobs in October when economists expected a gain, weeks after the RBA's fifth hike this year took the cash rate to 4.85%. It shifts the debate from more hikes to how long the RBA holds.

top.h: RBA minutes: the hike was a close call
top.d: Minutes released on 17 November show the board weighed a hike against a hold. The majority saw rising forward-looking inflation pressure; a minority wanted more time for earlier tightening to work.

top.h: ASIC sues CBA over alleged hidden CommBiz fees
top.d: ASIC alleges about 42,000 business customers were overcharged roughly $8.5 million in undisclosed fees. CBA says it has remediated and disputes parts of the case.

items.h: Westpac economists: Australia's labour market is no longer tight
items.d: October employment fell by about 43,500 and unemployment rose to 4.9% from 4.7%, according to Westpac's morning report. A separate Westpac economics update this month argues rates may have peaked, pointing to slower growth, higher unemployment and a housing market cooling faster than expected.
items.why: Your future employer's economists are signalling that the next RBA move is more likely a hold than a hike, which matters for margins and for mortgage credit quality.

sources.title: Westpac: Have interest rates hit their peak?

items.mention: Ask which parts of the Westpac economics team's rate view the business bank is already planning around.

items.h: Westpac's FY26 result: flat underlying profit, 77c final dividend
items.d: Westpac reported statutory net profit of about $6.8bn for the year to September, down 1%, and about $7.0bn excluding notable items, flat on FY25. The final dividend was 77 cents, a CET1 ratio of 12.5% sits above its 11.25% target, and business and institutional lending grew strongly.
items.why: This is the baseline your division is judged against: capital is comfortable, but growth is coming from business lending rather than profit expansion.

sources.title: Westpac FY26 result via Mirage News

items.h: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank over alleged undisclosed CommBiz fees
items.d: ASIC alleges CBA charged undisclosed 'contra leg' fees on direct debit and direct credit payments, affecting about 42,000 business customers and about $8.5 million between November 2020 and May 2025. CBA stopped charging in June 2025, has waived the fees since February 2026, and says it has paid over $26.4 million in remediation, while disputing some allegations.
items.why: Business banking fee disclosure is now a live enforcement area, which is directly relevant to Westpac's business bank.

items.h: RBA minutes show a debate between hiking and holding
items.d: Minutes of the 3-4 November meeting were published on 17 November. Coverage says members debated a 25bp rise against holding; the board delivered the hike on a 6-3 vote and dropped its explicit warning of further increases.
items.why: A split board and a data-dependent stance mean each jobs and CPI release now moves rate expectations.

items.h: APRA finalises its new bank licensing framework
items.d: APRA finalised outcomes-based licensing criteria for domestic bank applicants on 10 November, after consultations in 2025 and 2026. It is written into a legislative instrument rather than guidance.
items.why: Clearer licensing rules lower the barrier for new entrants, which is a long-run competitive threat to incumbents like Westpac.

background.h: Background: why super matters to a bank's wealth arm
background.d: The super guarantee has been 12% of ordinary earnings since 1 July 2025, so contributions flow into funds every pay cycle. Banks earn from this pool in three ways: platforms that hold investments, advice and adviser networks, and deposits and lending to members. When markets fall or regulation tightens, fee margins on platforms are what move. Nothing market-moving broke on super this morning, so treat this as groundwork.

background.h: Background: why small business loan margins are under pressure
background.d: An August 2026 Australian Banking Association report found the margin banks charge on small business loans above the cash rate is at a five-year low, which it puts down to strong competition. Non-bank lenders have also been gaining share, particularly on smaller loans, according to RBA research. The tension for a business banker: growth in lending is strong, but each dollar lent earns less.

items.h: Goldman trims its 2027 iron ore forecast as China's buying power grows
items.d: A 17 November report says Goldman Sachs cut its 2027 iron ore forecast to $92 a tonne from $96, and expects China's centralised buyer CMRG to gain pricing influence. Australia's Resources Minister has warned about the effect of that centralised purchasing.
items.why: Iron ore is Australia's largest export to China, so lower prices feed through to the budget, the AUD and mining-state credit quality.

items.h: Hong Kong passes banking legislation amendments
items.d: On 18 November the government welcomed the Legislative Council's passage of the Banking Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2026. The changes start phasing in from 1 January 2027.
items.why: It updates the rulebook for the banks you may eventually apply to; read the HKMA release for the specifics.

items.h: Citi's wealth head rules out big acquisitions, backs organic growth
items.d: A 17 November report says Citi's wealth chief Andy Sieg is focused on growing organically rather than buying. In May Citi said it would put a large share of its global wealth hiring into Asia, with roughly 100 private bankers and about 400 specialists planned.
items.why: Citi is a rival employer for wealth and Asia-facing roles, and the hiring plan shows where it is investing.

items.h: Fed minutes: October was a close call over a possible hike
items.d: Minutes published on 18 November for the 27-28 October meeting show the committee held rates but weighed raising them. Westpac's economists read the minutes as hawkish.
items.why: Higher-for-longer US rates support the US dollar and keep pressure on the AUD and on Australian funding costs.

primer.text: A written record of a central bank board's discussion, released about two weeks after the decision. It shows how close a vote was and what members were weighing.
Leaning toward higher interest rates to fight inflation. The opposite is dovish.
The gap between what a bank earns on loans and pays on funding, as a share of its earning assets. Competition on loan pricing squeezes it.
Court action in which a regulator such as ASIC asks for a fine rather than a criminal conviction. It is the main enforcement tool against corporate misconduct.

quiz.q: How did the RBA's board vote when it lifted the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November?
quiz.explain: Six members voted to hike and three to hold, and the statement dropped its earlier warning about further rises.

quiz.q: Why does a surprise jump in unemployment make further RBA hikes less likely?
options: A weaker labour market eases wage and inflation pressure
quiz.explain: Slack in the labour market reduces wage pressure and demand, so the RBA has less reason to tighten further.

quiz.q: What is ASIC alleging about CBA's CommBiz fees?
options: Undisclosed 'contra leg' fees were charged on direct debits and credits
quiz.explain: ASIC says terms did not clearly disclose a second fee on the matching leg of transfers, affecting about 42,000 business customers.

quiz.q: What does it mean that Fed minutes showed a 'close call over a possible hike'?
options: Some members seriously considered raising rates
quiz.explain: The committee held rates but a hike was a serious option, which is a hawkish signal for the US dollar.

quiz.q: Unemployment hit 4.9% weeks after the RBA hiked to 4.85%. In about 150 words, explain how this could affect a bank like Westpac through margins and credit quality, and name one indicator you would watch next.

chinese.english: Australia's central bank says most board members supported raising rates to 4.85%. Interest rates have become higher.

markets.summary: Unemployment rose to 4.9% in October, just after the RBA's fifth hike of 2026 took the cash rate to 4.85%, so debate has turned from more hikes to how long the RBA holds.
markets.forWestpac: A weaker labour market and falling house prices raise credit-quality questions for a mortgage-heavy bank, while a high-for-longer cash rate supports margins.
